Marquita Bradshaw

Democratic candidate for United States Senate, Tennessee · Challenger

Environmental justice advocate; runs the environmental nonprofit Sowing Justice (Memphis)

Marquita Bradshaw is an environmental justice advocate from Memphis who runs the nonprofit Sowing Justice. She was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Tennessee in 2020, losing to Bill Hagerty, and also ran for the Senate in 2024. She won the Democratic primary on August 6, 2026, which sets up a second general-election race against Hagerty.

Where Bradshaw stands

Immigration
Supports DACA and a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants. Says the U.S. should stop criminalizing and separating families seeking asylum. (Stated on her 2020 campaign site.)
Education
Has campaigned on competitive pay for teachers.
Housing
Has campaigned on affordable housing.
Health care
Has campaigned on affordable health care.
Rural broadband
Has campaigned on expanding broadband in rural areas.
Environment
Has campaigned on protecting Tennessee's natural resources.

Background

  • Born January 12, 1974, in Memphis, Tennessee
  • Education: B.L.S., University of Memphis
  • Environmental justice advocate; runs the nonprofit Sowing Justice
  • 2020: Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Tennessee; lost to Bill Hagerty
  • 2024: Candidate for U.S. Senate in Tennessee
  • 2026: Won the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate on August 6, 2026
